chunks: Regarding wiping: you wipe over the two sandals and do not insert your hand beneath the strap. And when you wipe with part of your head or with part of your feet, from between your ankle to the tips of the toes, that has sufficed you.

2- From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Shādhān ibn al-Khalīl al-Naysābūrī, from Yūnus, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥusayn.

He said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed wudu (ablution) while wearing a turban, and removing the turban was difficult for him because of the cold. So he said: Let him insert his finger.
3- As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

He said: I asked him about wiping over the feet, how it is. So he placed his palm on the toes and wiped them up to the ankles, over the upper part of the foot. I said: May I be your ransom, if a man were to say, with two fingers from his fingers, would that not suffice him? He said: No, no, it would not suffice him. So it is to be understood as pertaining to merit and recommendation, not obligation and requirement.
4- As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Bakr ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He said: When you perform wudu (ablution), wipe your feet, their upper and their lower sides. Then he said: Like this. So he placed his hand upon the ankle and struck the other upon the underside of his feet, then wiped them to the toes. The proper way to understand this report is what we mentioned in the previous chapter: that it is to be carried upon taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrine of some of the ʿāmmah who hold wiping over the two feet and say that the whole foot should be covered, and this is contrary to the truth as we have explained. That which also indicates what we have said is:
5- What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all of them from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah.

He said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Will you not inform me from where you knew and said that wiping is with part of the head and part of the two feet? So he laughed, then said: O Zurārah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said it, and the Book from Allah came down with it, because Allah says:
“So wash your faces.”
So we knew that the whole face is what he should wash. Then He said:
“And your hands up to the elbows.”
Then He separated between the two statements and said:
“And wipe your heads.”

So we knew, when He said: “with your heads,” that wiping is with part of the head because of the letter bā’. Then He joined the two feet to the head just as He joined the two hands to the face, so He said:
“And your feet up to the ankles.”

So we knew, when He joined them to the head, that wiping is with part of them. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم established that sunnah (prophetic tradition) for the people, but they neglected it. Then He said:
“But if you do not find water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, and wipe your faces and your hands from it.”

So when He lifted wudu (ablution) from the one who does not find water, He established part of washing as wiping, because He said: “with your faces and your hands from it.” Then He joined to it “and your hands.” Then He said: “from it,” meaning from that tayammum, because He knew that all of that does not pass over the face, since some of that earth adheres to part of the palm and does not adhere to another part of it. Then He said:
“Allah does not intend to place upon you in the religion any hardship.”
And al-ḥaraj means constriction.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in circumstances of pressure
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: the two feet that are to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the ankles, marking the extent mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.بِرُءُوسِكُمْ: the Quranic phrase indicating wiping of the head

ai.seo_question: How do the hadith and Quran indicate that wiping in wudu (ablution) is over part of the head and feet?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the rulings of wiping in wudu (ablution), especially wiping part of the head and feet, and supports that ruling through hadith and Quranic wording. It also explains that some reports are interpreted in light of taqiyyah, while the final narration presents an argument from the wording of the Quran for partial wiping and for ease in religion.
